name: Closed loop

subjectOf.text: The platform's feedback loop is closed in the sense that there are no rent seeking owners: the system is entirely supported by its users and the users reap the entire profit.
subjectOf.abstract: Therefore the feedback loop of the platform is closed, in the sense that there are no rent-seeking6 owners: The system is entirely supported by users, and the users reap the entire profit.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vlad Andrei, Blockchain Infrastructure for Measuring Domain Specific Reputation in Autonomous Decentralized and A (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3125822
scope_conditions: all fees are disbursed to expert users
no outside owner holds a claim on fees

subjectOf.text: The absence of fiat par-redemption combined with limited acceptance inside merchant ecosystems makes LER rewards closed-loop utilities, which is what removes their classification as electronic money tokens or securities.
subjectOf.abstract: Third, the absence of fiat par-redemption and limited acceptance within merchant ecosystems positions LER voucher loyalty rewards as closed-loop utilities. This removes their classification as electronic money tokens (EMTs) or securities, which, in turn, simplifys compliance.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054
scope_conditions: no redemption at par in fiat

subjectOf.text: Because LER vouchers are closed-loop and non-convertible, they reduce the risk of triggering FinCEN money services business registration and Bank Secrecy Act obligations that attach to convertible or transmissible digital value.
subjectOf.abstract: While convertible or transmissible digital value can trigger FinCEN MSB registration and BSA obligations, LER as closed-loop, non-convertible voucher rewards reduce that risk.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054

subjectOf.text: In the EU, MiCA exemptions for non-transferable utility tokens spare LER airdrops from white paper and issuer authorization requirements, but only so long as the rewards remain non-redeemable for fiat and confined to closed-loop merchant ecosystems.
subjectOf.abstract: In the EU, MiCA's exemptions for non-transferable utility tokens ensure that LER voucher rewards, distributed as airdrops, avoid white paper and issuer authorization requirements, as long as LER remain non-redeemable for fiat and confined to closed-loop merchant ecosystems.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054
scope_conditions: acceptance confined to closed-loop merchant networks

subjectOf.text: In the UK, e-money and payment services obligations attach if voucher rewards are fiat-redeemable or open-loop; otherwise LER should fall outside the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 and the Payment Services Regulations 2017 under limited-network concepts.
subjectOf.abstract: However, in the Uk, e-money and payments can arise if voucher rewards are fiat-redeemable or open-loop. Otherwise, LER are likely to avoid Electronic Money Regulations 2011 and Payment Services Regulations 2017 under limited-network concepts.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054

subjectOf.text: MiCA exempts non-transferable utility tokens like LER vouchers from white paper and issuer authorization requirements, but only while they lack investment characteristics and stay inside a closed-loop ecosystem.
subjectOf.abstract: MiCA exempts non-transferable utility tokens, such as LER's voucher rewards, from white paper and issuer authorization requirements, as long as they lack investment characteristics and are confined to closed-loop ecosystems.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards in Corporate America (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5583610

subjectOf.text: The HDCA settlement loop is closed in the topological sense: every job exits as resolved-validated or resolved-rejected and the system returns to a structurally identical state with only reputation scalars updated, so the set of possible actions never changes.
subjectOf.abstract: This is its central distinguishing feature relative to the HDCA settlement loop, which is closed in the topological sense: every job that enters the HDCA loop exits as either resolved-validated or resolved-rejected, and the system returns to a state structurally identical to where it began
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
